extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and U.S. Patent Office staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing receipt, filing, examination, amendment, appeal, interference handling, and ancillary matters (trade-marks, labels, reproduction) in U.S. patent practice as described by the 1878 Commissioner of Patents annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required parts of a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for letters patent, including the first or examination fee, the petition for a grant, the specification, drawing, and model, is received at the Patent Office either through the mail, by express, or by hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed parts (petition, specification, drawing, model) plus first/examination fee must accompany the application; delivery may be by mail, express, or hand. If any part is missing, applicant is notified and the application is not sent for examination until completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission handling and fee accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter sent by express is received by the machinist, who makes a daily record of the parts received, including fees, which latter are delivered daily to the financial clerk, who accounts for the same. When the application arrives by mail, or is delivered by hand, the fee is received by the financial clerk, the model is sent to the machinist, and the drawing and papers, with a memorandum of the fee, to the Application-room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct workflows for express vs mail/hand submissions: machinist labels/shelves models; financial clerk handles fees; daily records must be kept and fees promptly accounted for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application bibliographic and fee records
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Application-room an alphabetical record is made of all applications, showing the name of the applicant, his residence, the title of the invention, address of attorney, date of receipt of petition, affidavit, specification, drawing, model, and first fee, and the name of Examiner to whom it is sent. A separate account of fees received is also kept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File must include full bibliographic data and fee accounting; this record guides indorsing the application file-wrapper and tracking further letters/amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: File-wrapper stamping and index of case history
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Application-room the papers in each application receive the official stamp, indicating the day of their receipt, and are placed in a file-wrapper, upon which is indorsed the name and residence of the applicant, the subject of invention, the date of receipt of petition, affidavit, specification, drawing, and model, and the address of the attorney, if any there be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The file-wrapper must exhibit a complete index of the history of the case (dates and parts received) so that every official action and correspondence is traceable from the date of receipt in the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing inspection and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing is sent to the Drafting-division for inspection as to its mechanical execution. The draftsman places upon its back his stamp, and notes upon its face artistic defects, if any exist, and it is returned to the Application-room. Defects in the drawing may be corrected at anytime before final examination of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings are checked for mechanical/artistic execution; defects are annotated and may be corrected prior to final examination — ensure drawings meet mechanical execution standards to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model management and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The machinist labels the models, and shelves them until required in the examination of the application, having indorsed on the labels the applicant's name, the subject of invention, and the date of receipt. The model is delivered to the Examiner by the machinist as soon as required for examination, such delivery being noted upon the back of the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models must be properly labeled (name, subject, date) and shelf locations recorded so they can be retrieved and their delivery to Examiners tracked in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application is taken up for examination in the order of its receipt, excepting preferred cases specified in the statute and rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examinations proceed chronologically by receipt date unless specific statutory preference applies; applicants cannot expect out-of-order handling except where law/rules provide priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination for patentability and sufficiency of description
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination relates to the sufficiency of description and the patentability of the matter claimed, and requires a critical reading of the specification and a search through descriptions of prior inventions ... Such search is more or less extended according to the complexity of the invention and the antiquity of the art to which it pertains. It frequently requires, in single cases, the inspection of many hundred drawings and extended reading, occupying several days' time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners assess both sufficiency of disclosure and novelty/non-obviousness by searching domestic and foreign patents and printed publications; more complex or older arts demand deeper searches. About fifteen percent of completed applications are allowed without objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must particularly and distinctly point out the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If upon examination it appears that the matter specified is patentable, and that it is well and sufficiently described, and that it is particularly and distinctly pointed out in the claim, the application is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must clearly and distinctly define the invention; sufficiency of specification and claim clarity are prerequisites for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for formal defects and missing parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If, as often occurs, the application appears on its face to be defective in form, or if any part is wholly wanting, applicant is notified. Upon completion of the application in proper form, the drawing and file are immediately sent for examination as to patentability to the division to which it pertains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will not proceed to substantive examination until formal defects/missing elements are cured; applicants must respond to notices to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of rejection and applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If, however, the application is rejected, the Commissioner of Patents, by the Examiner, causes the applicant to be informed of the reasons of such rejection, and to be furnished with pertinent information for his guidance as to the further prosecution of the application. Applicant may respond to such rejection by a request for reconsideration with or without amendment of his specification, and he may ask a reconsideration as often as new references are cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections are accompanied by reasons and guidance; applicants may request reconsideration and amend repeatedly as new references are cited — multiple rejections are common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for written amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Written amendments of a specification are entered as follows: Matter to be inserted is inclosed by lines on the amendment, and the place of insertion, as stated by applicant, marked on the body of the specification. Matter to be erased from the specification is inclosed by lines and canceled. Similar reference letters are placed on the amendment and on the specification at the place where it is to be entered, and said letters are indorsed on the back of the amendment. Red ink is used for distinctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must follow the specified marking conventions (insertions/erasures marked, reference letters, red ink) to be properly entered; complex amendments may exhaust reference letters and be numerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of correspondence and official actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Every official communication by the Examiner in an application, and every communication from the applicant or his attorney, is placed in the file and noted upon the back of the file-wrapper in proper order and time, and said wrapper exhibits a complete index of the history of the case from the date of its receipt in the Office. Every official action by the Examiner is duly noted in his register adjacent to the original entry of the application, and all official letters are copied by press into a letter-book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain comprehensive, chronological records in the file-wrapper and registers; copy official letters into letter-books to preserve an auditable history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application numbering and registry entries
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Examiner's room the application is registered and numbered. The registry entry includes the date of the receipt by the Examiner of the application, the name of the applicant, the subject of invention, the monthly number, and, usually, an attorney's name and the location (shelf) of model. The register number is placed upon the file-wrapper, drawing, and model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign and record a unique register number and related metadata; ensure the number is marked on all physical parts to maintain linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference declaration and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When an interference is found to exist between two or more cases the applications are delayed, if practicable without injustice, until each is put in condition for allowance in case it receives award of priority of invention. Upon declaration of preliminary interference by the Examiner the several parties or their attorneys ... are notified of the interference, of the names of the parties to the same and their attorneys, and of the residences of both, and of the interfering subject-matter, and of the claims in each case embracing such matter. The Examiner of Interferences fixes the time of filing preliminary statements therein and causes the copies of letters furnished him to be mailed to the appropriate parties. After decision by the Examiner of Interferences as to priority, upon evidence and argument, or after final adjudication upon appeal, the files and papers are returned to the Examiner, who sends the application of the successful party to issue, unless such party is already a patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference process includes formal notification, preparation of interference files, schedule for preliminaries, potential delay of issuance until parties are in condition for allowance, and appeal rights; strict procedural compliance is required in preliminary declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If any one of the statutory bars ... is found to exist upon examination ... then an appeal may be taken from such adverse decision to the Board of Examiners-in-Chief, and from an adverse decision of the Board to the Commissioner in person. Any party to an interference, against whom an adverse finding of priority has been rendered, may appeal from the judgment of the Examiner of Interferences to the Board of Examiners-in-Chief, and from an adverse decision of the Board to the Commissioner in person. Every other question or dispute ... is appealable, after adverse decision, directly to the Commissioner. The filing of an appeal is recorded in the Application-room, and the written reasons of appeal placed in a file-wrapper and sent to the proper Examiner, who makes written answer to the same and sends the application and the appeal-file containing reasons and answer to the clerk in charge of appeal-files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various appeal routes exist (Board of Examiners-in-Chief, Commissioner); appeals must be recorded with written reasons; Examiners prepare written answers and appeal-files are managed by a clerk — parties should follow formal appeal filing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of appeals and interlocutory matters
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal to the Commissioner in an interlocutory matter no separate file is kept, but the reasons and answer are inserted in the application-file. After a final adjudication by the Board of Examiners-in-Chief, or by the Commissioner of Patents, or the Supremo Court of the District of Columbia upon further appeal, the application, appeal papers, and decision are returned to the Examiner, who allows the application with or without amendment, or files it among rejected cases according to the tenor of said decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory appeals are folded into the application file; final adjudications result in allowance (possibly with amendment) or filing among rejected cases. Maintain comprehensive documentation of the decision trail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-mark and label registration processing and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trade-mark division records cases on hand, trade-marks received, labels received, amended cases, and actions made. Amount derived from trade-mark applications is tracked (e.g., amount from applications upon which full fees have been paid and upon which first fee has been paid). The work of the division includes printing trade-mark specifications and certificates, and requires clerical help for preparing certificates. The division's staffing and salary estimates are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade-mark/label filings are counted and fees tracked (first fee vs full fee); issuance of certificates and registration actions are processed and staffing/costs estimated — applicants must pay the required fee level (first fee or full fee) to trigger particular processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and reproduction of old patents (printing and photolithography)
rubrics_metrics.description: The printing of patents dates from November 20, 1866 ... there remain about 58,000 recorded patents unprinted. All the original drawings accompanying these patents have been reproduced by the photolithographic process. It is estimated that the cost of printing the 58,000 specifications will amount to $230,000. The completion of the reproduction of all the old drawings has considerably reduced the demand for manuscript copies of their accompanying specifications. Were these printed the salaries of six copyists and two comparers, amounting to the annual sum of $7,400, would be saved to the Office. The advantage to be afforded the Office and the public ... in the examination of applications ... and the dissemination of knowledge of the state of the art in every class of inventions would be extensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce and print historic specifications and drawings to (1) preserve originals from wear, (2) reduce ongoing copyist labor and expense, and (3) make prior art more accessible for examination and public dissemination; cost-benefit estimates should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistics and reporting metrics for Office activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The report tabulates counts for: Applications for patents (including designs), Applications for reissue, Patents issued (including designs), Patents reissued, Patents extended, Caveats filed, Patents expired, Patents withheld for non-payment of final fee, Applications for registration of trade-marks, Trade-marks registered, Applications for registration of labels, Labels registered, and number of patents by State/Territory and by foreign subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and publish comprehensive statistics (applications, issuances, reissues, trade-marks, labels, geographic distribution, receipts/expenditures) to inform Congress, the public, and internal planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of inter-office and external copies and searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination requires a search through descriptions of prior inventions pertaining to the same subject found in the specifications and drawings of domestic and foreign patents, and in other printed publications, or in manuscript digests of the same. Such search is more or less extended according to the complexity of the invention and the antiquity of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must use available domestic and foreign patent collections, printed publications, and manuscript digests; ensure access to complete sets and indexes (including foreign patent exchanges) to perform thorough prior art searches.
